characterList.description: Thin, blue, thread-like structures inside the cell nucleus.
characterList.name: Chromatin

characterList.description: Short, thick, X-shaped blue structures, formed from condensed chromatin.
characterList.name: Chromosomes

characterList.description: Two identical halves of a chromosome, joined together at the centromere.
characterList.name: Sister Chromatids

characterList.description: The red dot that joins the two sister chromatids.
characterList.name: Centromere

characterList.description: Yellow starburst-shaped structures with multiple arms that form the spindle.
characterList.name: Centrosomes

characterList.description: Two small yellow cylinders within the centrosome.
characterList.name: Centrioles

characterList.description: A network of yellow lines radiating from the centrosomes.
characterList.name: Spindle

characterList.description: The separated sister chromatids, each now considered an individual chromosome.
characterList.name: Daughter Chromosomes

characterList.description: A small, yellow sphere inside the nucleus.
characterList.name: Nucleolus

characterList.description: A transparent membrane surrounding the nucleus.
characterList.name: Nuclear Membrane

characterList.description: The orange gel-like substance filling the cell.
characterList.name: Cytoplasm

characterList.description: A groove that forms in the plasma membrane of an animal cell during cytokinesis.
characterList.name: Cleavage Furrow

characterList.description: A structure that forms in the center of a plant cell during cytokinesis, eventually becoming a new cell wall.
characterList.name: Cell Plate

characterList.description: The green hexagonal outline surrounding the plant cell.
characterList.name: Cell Wall

characterList.description: The two identical cells resulting from mitosis and cytokinesis.
characterList.name: Daughter Cells

content_metadata.description: A detailed analysis and breakdown of the process of mitosis as depicted in various scenes of a video.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the red structure that joins the two sister chromatids?

qAndA.answer: Microtubules from the spindle interact with the kinetochores on the chromosomes, pulling them towards the equatorial plate. (1:36 - 1:45)
qAndA.question: How do chromosomes align in the middle of the cell during metaphase?

qAndA.answer: The nuclear membrane starts to break down. (1:16)
qAndA.question: What happens to the nuclear membrane during prophase?

qAndA.answer: Animal cells form a cleavage furrow that deepens to divide the cell, while plant cells form a cell plate in the center that grows outwards to become a new cell wall. (3:01 - 3:33)
qAndA.question: What is the key difference in cytokinesis between animal cells and plant cells?

qAndA.answer: It was included to illustrate that mitosis is essential for the regeneration of body parts, which is a key function of this cell division process. (0:06 - 0:13)
qAndA.question: Why was the lizard animation included in the video about mitosis?

youtube_description: Mitosis is a process of nuclear division in eukaryotic cells that occurs when a parent cell divides to produce two identical daughter cells. During cell division, mitosis refers specifically to the separation of the duplicated genetic material carried in the nucleus. Mitosis is conventionally divided into five stages known as prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase. While mitosis is taking place, there is no cell growth and all of the cellular energy is focused on cell division.
